name: THE LANE
note: EXTRACTED by tools/extract-examine.mjs from the documents its sources name -- errata 67's merge, in doc 05's, the batch's, then the repeats' order, less errata 68 H's drops. Do not edit: change the documents and re-run.

subjects.name: THE LANE ITSELF
LOOK_AT: The Lane: the street the town keeps for the businesses it doesn't put on the main one.
Wide enough for two men to pass, provided they have agreed on something first.
Puddles all the way down, each one holding a lamp. It is the best-lit the Lane will ever be.
LISTEN_TO: Main Street at one end, Lower Street at the other, and in between a hush you could rent.
A shutter knocking, then thinking better of it.
The tent's canvas, breathing, two doors down. The Lane has a pulse and it's hers.

subjects.name: THE COFFIN BY THE DOOR
LOOK_AT: A pine coffin standing on end by the undertaker's door, like a man waiting to be let in.
Plain pine, nicely planed. Somebody is going to be very comfortable in that.
Standard length. A tall man would have to be very patient in it.
LISTEN_TO: Hollow. A good coffin rings like a cello, and this one rings like a cheap cello.
Nothing inside. I checked by knocking, and then felt I ought to apologize.
The wind across the open end, making the only sound a coffin is allowed.

overrides.PICK_UP: It's stock. Taking it would be stealing from the one merchant whose customers never complain.
overrides.OPEN: Empty, and planed smooth inside. I closed it gently. You do.

subjects.name: THE PHOTOGRAPHER'S WINDOW
LOOK_AT: The photographer's window. In the middle of it, a portrait of a distinguished gentleman in a very good collar, lit like a saint.
The gentleman in the portrait has a face you would trust with your money, which in this town is a professional qualification.
Portraits by appointment. I can't afford the appointment, but I could stand here and be photographed by accident.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. The gentleman in the window has been holding very still for a long time.
A clock inside, very slow, as if it were sitting for its portrait.
Glass plates clinking in the back, being careful with each other.

overrides.TALK_TO: I asked the gentleman in the portrait for directions. He kept his counsel, and his collar.

subjects.name: OZYMANDIA'S TENT
LOOK_AT: Madame Ozymandia's tent, painted with more stars than the sky can spare.
The flap is tied back and candlelight comes out. It is the most inviting door in Consolation, which is why I keep a hand on my pocket.
The stars on the canvas don't quite line up with the ones above it. Neither, I suspect, do the predictions.
LISTEN_TO: Humming, low and long, from inside. Either a lady concentrating or a lady charging.
A brass rod, set down carefully on a table.
The canvas moving with the wind. It sounds like the tent is thinking about me.

overrides.PUSH: You don't push a fortune-teller's tent. She'll have seen it coming, and she'll charge.

subjects.name: THE BARBER'S POLE
LOOK_AT: A barber's pole, painted to look as though it turns. It doesn't. That is the first lie a barber tells you.
There's a light under the door. A barber-surgeon in a mining camp keeps a doctor's hours.
I could do with a shave. I could do with the price of a shave more.
LISTEN_TO: The pole creaking in its bracket. It would turn if it could.
A strop swaying on its hook inside, slapping the chair once.
Nothing. A barber's shop is never quiet by day; at night it makes up for it.

overrides.TALK_TO: I asked for a trim. The pole said nothing, which is more than most barbers manage.

subjects.name: THE EMPTY STOREFRONT
LOOK_AT: An empty storefront, boarded, its sign painted out. Somebody's whole idea, closed for good.
Through a gap in the boards: dark, and a smell of old sawdust. Whatever was sold here, it sold out.
If I strike it rich, I'll buy this and sell something. I don't yet know what. In Consolation that has never stopped anybody.
LISTEN_TO: A loose board, lifting and settling with the wind.
Nothing. The quiet of a shop with nothing to sell and nobody to sell it.

overrides.OPEN: Boarded with long nails, by somebody who meant it.
